$comment: Lane 12 item 4: one entry per dataset downloaded into home/data-scratch/datasets/ (git-ignored, never copied into the tracked tree, never shipped). sha256 values are copied from data-scratch/datasets/SHA256SUMS, the checksums this repo's own download actually produced (org rule: never trusted from a listing). `loader` names the module in this directory that reads it, or null for a dataset with no loader yet (downloaded for a later item - the phenomenon-mining sources, ACT-02's emotion-head training data). `heldOut` names the split this project reserves and never samples questions or scenarios from, so a later item's prompt-writing or tuning cannot see what the eval checks.

datasets.name: longmemeval-cleaned
datasets.attribution: Wu et al., "LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory", ICLR 2025.
datasets.collectionMethod: Synthetic long-term chat histories assembled by the paper's authors (GPT-4-authored sessions plus real ShareGPT-derived filler sessions as distractors), with hand-authored and verified questions over six question types.
datasets.holdsRealIdentitiesNote: The filler/distractor sessions in the S set are drawn from ShareGPT, real (if pseudonymous) user-model conversations shared publicly by their authors - treated conservatively as holding real identities even though the questions and answer-bearing sessions themselves are synthetic.
datasets.heldOut: none named by the paper; this project holds out the ids NOT in sample-manifest.json (sample.ts's own selection) from any prompt-writing or tuning session, per the coherence review's rule.

datasets.name: longmemeval-cleaned-m
datasets.attribution: Wu et al., "LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory", ICLR 2025.
datasets.collectionMethod: Same as longmemeval-cleaned, with a larger distractor pool per question (the paper's own "M" haystack size).
datasets.holdsRealIdentitiesNote: Same ShareGPT-derived filler sessions as the S set, at a larger scale.
datasets.heldOut: not sampled by this item at all (the S set's own 500 questions already cover every question id the M set reuses); kept only in case a future item needs the larger haystack.

datasets.name: locomo
datasets.version: locomo10 (the ten publicly released of the paper's fifty)
datasets.attribution: Maharana et al., "Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents", 2024 (Snap Research).
datasets.collectionMethod: Fully synthetic: LLM agents role-playing two generated personas over up to 35 dated sessions, with hand-verified question-answer pairs across five question categories.
datasets.heldOut: none named by the paper; this project treats the whole released set as eval-only (ingested whole per the coherence review, never used to tune a prompt).

datasets.name: dailydialog
datasets.attribution: Li et al., "DailyDialog: A Manually Labelled Multi-turn Dialogue Dataset", IJCNLP 2017.
datasets.collectionMethod: Dialogues drawn from English-practice websites for everyday conversation, manually labelled with a dialogue act and an emotion per turn.
datasets.heldOut: the test split (test.zip) is never used for register-reference sampling in this project, only train and validation.

datasets.name: taskmaster-1
datasets.attribution: Byrne et al., "Taskmaster-1: Toward a Realistic and Diverse Dialog Dataset", EMNLP 2019 (Google Research).
datasets.collectionMethod: Crowdsourced: self-dialogs written solo by one crowdworker playing both sides; woz-dialogs collected two-crowdworker Wizard-of-Oz sessions.
datasets.heldOut: lane 13 item 1's mine.ts reads this whole file (both self-dialogs and woz-dialogs) to select phenomenon fragments for a person's review; no item samples scenarios from it yet - that rewrite step lands after CHAT-16 (docs/plans/session-b-lane-13-2026-09-14.md).

datasets.name: ccpe-m
datasets.attribution: Radlinski et al., "Coached Conversational Preference Elicitation", SIGdial 2019 (Google Research).
datasets.collectionMethod: Crowdsourced: two workers per session, one coached to elicit the other's movie preferences.
datasets.heldOut: lane 13 item 1's mine.ts reads this whole file to select preference fragments for a person's review; no item samples scenarios from it yet - that rewrite step lands after CHAT-16 (docs/plans/session-b-lane-13-2026-09-14.md).

datasets.name: multiwoz
datasets.license: MIT (repository); see the dataset's own README for the data license
datasets.attribution: Eric et al., "MultiWOZ 2.1: A Consolidated Multi-Domain Dialogue Dataset with State Corrections and State Tracking Baselines", LREC 2020.
datasets.heldOut: not sampled by any item yet; downloaded for the phenomenon-mining item (mixed intents and topic switches), which lands after CHAT-16.

datasets.name: quac
datasets.attribution: Choi et al., "QuAC: Question Answering in Context", EMNLP 2018.
datasets.collectionMethod: Crowdsourced: a student asks free-form questions about a Wikipedia section, a teacher (with access to the article) answers with a quoted span.
datasets.heldOut: val_v0.2.json is treated as this project's held-out split; lane 13 item 1's mine.ts reads train_v0.2.json only, to select phenomenon fragments for a person's review.

datasets.name: goemotions
datasets.attribution: Demszky et al., "GoEmotions: A Dataset of Fine-Grained Emotions", ACL 2020 (Google Research).
datasets.collectionMethod: Real Reddit comments, filtered for length and profanity, hand-labelled with fine-grained emotion categories by crowdworkers.
datasets.holdsRealIdentitiesNote: Real (pseudonymous) Reddit users' own public comments, not synthetic or crowdworker-authored text - the one dataset in this registry that is real social-media speech rather than a constructed dialogue.
datasets.heldOut: test.tsv is treated as this project's held-out split; train.tsv/dev.tsv only are used for the emotion head's own training data (ACT-02, ahead of this item).
